solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nice bit of fluff? Don't whistle, that's rude!

indicators.note: rude here means rough or crudely made, so the letters of the phrase are roughly reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for an impolite whistle at a pretty sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges the letters of DONT WHISTLE; the question mark signals the cheeky 'nice bit of fluff' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The downy seed tufts of a thistle are a classic example of pleasant, floating fluff.

clue.text: One of many carried by the caddy

definitions.text: One of many carried by the caddy

parts.words: One of many carried by the caddy
parts.note: a golf caddy carries clubs, but the container meant is a tea caddy, whose contents are many dried leaves

explanation.surface: A golf caddy lugs a bag holding many clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caddy' points to golf, but a tea caddy is a tin for tea; in British rhyming slang the answer also means a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a storage tin holding many dried leaves for brewing.

clue.text: One wise man's got the picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a magus or wise man

explanation.surface: One of the Magi has taken a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a visual representation, the same thing as a picture.

clue.text: Entrance for vehicles

definitions.meaning: to entrance is to enrapture or carry away with delight
cars, buses and trains collectively are a means of conveyance

explanation.surface: A sign marks the way in for cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a noun (a way in) but is the verb, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to enrapture someone, and the system of conveyances.

clue.text: This way for a place? You bet!

definitions.text: This way for a place? You bet!

parts.words: This way for a place? You bet!
parts.note: in horse racing a bet laid this way pays out if the horse wins or merely finishes placed

explanation.surface: Someone asks directions to a spot and gets an enthusiastic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet covers both a win and a place; the clue reads like asking directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the betting phrase for a wager on a horse to win or finish placed.

clue.text: Gloomy, although recovered from eye problem

parts.note: to be over an illness is to have recovered from it
a cast is a squint in the eye

explanation.surface: Someone stays glum even after getting better from an eye complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and cloudy, which is gloomy weather.

clue.text: The fall that followed Eve

parts.note: the Fall of the Bible came after Eve, but here eve is evening, and the fall that comes after it is the onset of darkness

explanation.surface: A reference to the biblical Fall after Eve ate the apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve is evening, not Adam's wife; nightfall follows evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is when darkness arrives, following on from the evening.

clue.text: Performer tires at appearing in variety

indicators.note: variety suggests a different mixture, so these letters are rearranged; it also plays on variety shows

explanation.surface: A music-hall act grows weary of appearing in variety shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, especially a singer or dancer on stage.

clue.text: Not free of tax but ideal otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A purchase would be ideal, except that duty must be paid on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are dutiable attract customs duty, so they are taxed rather than exempt.

clue.text: A snowdrop?

parts.note: not the spring flower but snow literally dropping down a mountainside in a mass

explanation.surface: A one-word reference to the small white winter flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snowdrop' wants to be the flower; read it as a drop of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow falling down a mountain slope.

clue.text: Pinched note to relative

parts.note: G is a musical note
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A brief message is sent to a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinched face is thin and drawn, which is the haggard look of a gaunt person.

clue.text: Very strange verse on love

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so these letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A poem about romance is described as bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase is an intensifier meaning extremely, as in 'so kind'.

clue.text: Explorer is eating last of sledge dogs

parts.note: Captain Scott was the Antarctic explorer

indicators.note: eating means the word is takes in another letter, swallowing it
last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A polar explorer consumes the final part of his sledge dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sledge dogs' tempts as one phrase; the explorer is Captain Scott of the Antarctic, which suits the sledging surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotties are Scottish terriers, a breed of small dog.

clue.text: Don went down with a cry of pain

parts.note: fell is the past tense of fall, to go down
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A man collapsed, yelping in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Don is a university teacher, not the verb or name.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford or Cambridge a fellow is a senior member of a college, which is a don.

clue.text: Spring's finished, that's clear

parts.note: spring as a verb means to jump, a leap (the 's read as 'is')
over means finished or ended

explanation.surface: The spring season has ended, which is quite plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season; it is a jump. 'clear' is a verb, as in clearing a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear an obstacle is to jump over it without touching it.

clue.text: Bless me! A boisterous get-together

definitions.note: a hyphenated noun for a party, but read as the verb phrase 'get together', meaning to gather, which matches a verb answer

indicators.note: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a rowdy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-together' reads as a party but is the verb to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather in one place, which is to come together.

clue.text: Crank, socially and mechanically

parts.note: an odd person is a crank, and in engineering an off-centre disc that converts motion is a kind of crank too

explanation.surface: A description of a crackpot in society and in machines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unconventional oddball and an off-centre rotating disc in machinery.

clue.text: One whose pictures attract lots of admiration

definitions.text: One whose pictures attract lots of admiration

parts.words: One whose pictures attract lots of admiration
parts.note: sounds like a painter, but pictures are movies and the person admired stars in them

explanation.surface: A painter whose work wins wide praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pictures' suggests paintings; it means films, and the admired person appears in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated cinema actor is adored by fans for appearing in movies.

clue.text: Sort of banana has insect visible on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means one word wraps around the other, surrounding it

parts.note: plain means clear to see, visible
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A banana with a bug crawling clearly on its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy cooking variety of banana.

clue.text: Ill-mannered person with dog in queue

parts.note: a rude or greedy person is called a pig
to dog someone is to follow them, tail

explanation.surface: A rude man stands in line with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queue' is an old word for a plait of hair hanging down the back, not a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is a braid of hair worn hanging behind, the same thing as a plait.

clue.text: It smoothly finishes off a piece of writing

definitions.meaning: a levelling layer of cement or the tool that smooths a floor's top coat
a long, often tedious written passage

explanation.surface: Something that polishes off an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders lay a smooth floor topping by this name, and it also means a long tract.

clue.text: Fed up with being exploited and rendered ineffective

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: used means exploited

explanation.surface: Someone tired of being taken advantage of has been neutralised.
explanation.definitionFit: A defused bomb has had its detonator removed so it can no longer harm.

clue.text: Suitable moment for some fun

explanation.surface: Choosing the right moment to enjoy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an opportune occasion and also an enjoyable spell of fun.

clue.text: Act as a paid informer

parts.note: sounds like a police grass, but the informing is passing on knowledge as a job

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to snitch to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informer' suggests a spy; a teacher informs pupils for a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructing pupils for pay is imparting information as a profession.

clue.text: Individual away from work, just this once

parts.note: one means a single individual
to be off is to be absent from work

explanation.surface: A worker takes a single day off.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off event happens only on a single occasion.

clue.text: Open-air party is best

parts.note: out means outdoors, in the open air
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An outdoor party is the finest kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb here, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best a rival is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: A pound's put on for services

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight, and the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight to be ready for duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' are church services: albs are worn by clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white vestment that clergy wear when leading church worship.

clue.text: Region holding northern sports venue

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other inside it

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: A northern region has a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space where sporting contests are held.

clue.text: Allows real changes in better systems

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the betting word

parts.note: a tote is a betting system for punters, so totes are betting systems

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Genuine reforms are allowed in improved systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is someone who bets: the tote is a pool betting system. 'changes' makes LERA from REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to put up with it, to allow it.

clue.text: Instrument posh Richard played

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-to-do man performed on a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpsichord is a keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked.
